details: Iranian Army Chief Commander Amir Hatami announced that U.S. forces have been expelled from the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and the strategic Strait of Hormuz, stating they are prohibited from returning. Hatami emphasized that U.S. military bases in the region could not revert to their previous state and Iran would not allow their reestablishment. This declaration comes amidst heightened tensions as a 60-day US-Iran ceasefire agreement expired.
title: Iran Declares Expulsion of U.S. Forces from Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz

details: A 60-day interim agreement between the United States and Iran, intended to end the war and facilitate negotiations, officially expired on August 17 without an extension. Both nations remain at an impasse, particularly concerning control over the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively closed. Iran maintains that the strait remains under its full control and will only be opened under its command, rejecting U.S. claims of control.
title: US-Iran Ceasefire Expires Amid Impasse Over Strait of Hormuz

details: Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law and Middle East envoy, held a rare direct meeting with Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo on Sunday. The discussions focused on a U.S.-backed peace plan for Gaza, which calls for Hamas's disarmament and an Israeli military withdrawal. Despite the meeting, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly rejected the 15-point roadmap.
title: Hamas Leader Meets Jared Kushner for Gaza Peace Talks in Cairo

details: Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz has instructed the military to prepare a plan to transfer all civilian enforcement authority for Israeli communities and residents in the West Bank from the army to the Israel Police. This move is seen by some as a step towards further annexation of the occupied Palestinian territory and has raised concerns among Palestinian factions.
title: Israel to Transfer West Bank Civilian Enforcement from Army to Police
